title: Bank loan-to-value limits: the value the ratio runs on
rule: National banks, FDIC-supervised banks and state member banks must keep written real estate lending policies with loan-to-value limits, considering interagency guidelines. The guidelines tell each bank to set internal limits no higher than supervisory limits (85 percent for improved property), list excluded transactions, and allow exception loans within aggregate caps. The ratio, set at origination, is the loan plus senior liens over the property's value plus other acceptable collateral. Value is market value estimated in an appraisal or evaluation; for a loan to buy an existing property, it is the lesser of the actual acquisition cost and that estimate. An appraisal above the contract price does not raise the base.
